content:
devon: ops-bot alert: eu-central GPU capacity degraded, 60% of pods pending due to resource provisioning errors. seeing quota failures from cloud side. :eyes:
ops-bot: [ALERT] gpu-provisioner: failure_rate=0.62, pending_pods=124, region=eu-central
alex: ack. are we talking NVidia quota or instance-type shortage?
maria: looks like instance availability spike. cloud console shows capacity constrained for a few SKUs (a100-v4). provisioning API is returning 503 intermittently.
leah: can we shift traffic to euc1-burst / reserve pools? what's the risk on latency?
devon: we did a weighted shift to sfo-edge and ams in the last 2 mins (manual override). initial telemetry shows 120ms median increase for some routes, but error rate dropped.
samir: good. any automated fallback kicked in? I don't see circuit-breaker entries in the dashboard.
maria: circuit breaker didn't trigger because provisioning errors were classified as transient. need to update rule to consider quota-503 as hard-failure for booking.
alex: agree. current rule only looks at 5xx from runtime, not provider-level 503s. we should include cloud-provisioner error codes.
leah: ops action item: update failover playbook to include: pre-warm warm-pool for critical SKUs during regional business hours; escalate to dedicated capacity if pending_pods > 50 for > 3m; treat cloud-provisioner 5xx as immediate failover trigger.
devon: also add a step to check "reserved instance hooks" in the cloud console — there was a dangling reservation that blocked provisioning in one AZ. filed a ticket with cloud support.
ops-bot: ticket created: CSP-8421 referencing region eu-central SKU contention.
samir: cost note — aggressive pre-warming/dedicated shifts will increase monthly committed spend. propose adding a cost-guardrails section to playbook: default to bursting only up to 20% of baseline for 30m, require approvals above threshold.
maria: propose we add a quick command snippet to the playbook to re-route via weighted policy. add to runbook:
```
# shift 30% traffic from eu-central to ams and sfo
rctl route shift --from eu-central --to ams,sfo --weights 0.15,0.15 --cooldown 300
```
leah: also include telemetry sanity checks after shift: token-p99 latency, error-rate, spiky queue length. we should make those checks automated as a playbook step.
alex: itemize post-incident tasks: 1) update circuit-breaker rules (alex) 2) add pre-warm schedule + owner (leah) 3) add cost guardrail thresholds to playbook + approval flow (samir) 4) add cloud-provisioner error mappings to alerting (maria) 5) follow-up with CSP on reservation leakage (devon).
devon: assigning owners in triage board now. will drop links to PRs and runbook edits here when created.
leah: quick reality check: do we want an emergency knob to temporarily suspend model rollouts or large batch jobs during region stress? that would reduce pressure.
samir: yes, add a step: suspend non-critical batch workloads (label: batch-optional) and block new heavy allocations. need a one-line command in playbook.
maria: adding sample suspend command:
```
kubectl label nodepool eu-central batch-eligibility=disabled --overwrite
kubectl scale deployment big-training-job --replicas=0 -n batch-jobs
```
ops-bot: reminder: please attach any PRs to incident ticket CSP-8421 for audit.
alex: timeline note for postmortem: incident start 2234567890, initial manual shift at 2234567920, cloud quota error resolved and normal provisioning resumed at 2234567940.
leah: good. i'll draft playbook patch with the new checklist and add screenshots for where to find the reservation hooks.
devon: thanks team. let's keep the follow-ups in a dedicated thread after the incident to avoid noise here. :thumbsup:
